  # What is waiting to land?
  gz-git integrate queue

  # Is this branch ready?
  gz-git integrate check

  # Fast-forward the target and reclaim the task branch
  gz-git integrate run

integrate answers a different question than branch list. queue lists
unfinished task branches, check is the readiness gate, and run
fast-forwards then reclaims. gz-git builds, runs, and lints no
repository code: git checks alone decide readiness.

Each repository and target ref has its own Git target lock. A command
waits for it until the lock is free or the command is interrupted.

Usage:
  gz-git integrate [command]

Available Commands:
  check          Verify a task branch is ready to integrate
  cleanup        Cleanup-only retry for an evidenced integrate run
  legacy-cleanup Plan or apply prospective legacy cleanup
  provision      Provision declared local sibling dependencies
  queue          List unfinished task branches
  receipt        Read the durable integrate receipt for one execution
  reconcile      Attest a bounded legacy pre-mutation refusal
  run            Fast-forward integrate and reclaim the task branch

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for integrate

Global Flags:
      --profile string   override active profile (e.g., --profile work)
  -q, --quiet            quiet output (errors only)
  -v, --verbose          verbose output

Use "gz-git integrate [command] --help" for more information about a command.
"

  # Check the current branch against the integration branch
  gz-git integrate check

  # Required when no integration branch can be resolved
  gz-git integrate check --target origin/main --direct-to-default

This is read-only. It never pushes and never reclaims.
gz-git builds, executes and lints no repository code. The gate mode is
always "none": the git checks alone (freshness, merge-tree, other branches,
clean working tree, pushed source, post-gate revalidation) decide READY.
Run a bare check from a task-branch worktree, not from the target checkout.

Engine: gz-git-integrate (Go)

Exit Codes:
  0  READY
  1  NOT READY, or --target required
  2  the check itself could not run
  4  --expect-source/--expect-target: the approved commit pair changed

Usage:
  gz-git integrate check [branch] [flags]

Effect: mutating (tracking-refs, filesystem)

Flags:
      --controller-config string   explicit devbox/controller config; never searched automatically
      --direct-to-default          allow targeting the default branch when no integration branch exists
      --expect-source string       fail with exit 4 unless the source is this full commit SHA
      --expect-target string       fail with exit 4 unless the target is this full commit SHA
  -h, --help                       help for check
      --no-fetch                   resolve the target from local tracking refs without fetching
      --release                    promote the integration branch onto the default branch
      --target string              integration target (required when none can be resolved)

Global Flags:
      --profile string   override active profile (e.g., --profile work)
  -q, --quiet            quiet output (errors only)
  -v, --verbose          verbose output
"
    },
    {
      "command": "gz-git",
      "executable": "<SANDBOX>/bin/gz-git",
      "args": [
        "integrate",
        "run",
        "--help"
      ],
      "cwd": "<SANDBOX>/repo",
      "exitCode": 0,
      "stdout": " Quick Start:
  # Integrate the current branch
  gz-git integrate run

  # Required when no integration branch can be resolved
  gz-git integrate run --target origin/main --direct-to-default

  # Durable evidence for an external task runtime (TASK-302): all context
  # flags together, --expect-source included, or none of them
  gz-git integrate run --execution-id run-42 --generation g7 \
    --owner-actor claude --owner-host mbp --owner-kind agent \
    --expect-source <full-sha> --json

Reclaim only runs for names matching the repo-root taskPattern.
No declaration means reclaim nothing. Remote branch delete uses
--force-with-lease against the commit that just landed.
Run a bare integrate from a task-branch worktree, not from the target checkout.

Execution context (--execution-id, --generation, --owner-actor, --owner-host,
--owner-kind, plus --expect-source) records a durable receipt under the Git
common dir (gz-integrate/v1, receipt schema_version 2) before the push: intent, then pushed, then the
reclaim results. The identity is immutable — reusing an execution-id with a
different generation/owner/repo/task/target, push endpoint or protections
fails before pushing. Legacy v1 receipts are read-only. With
--json, run prints the machine protocol document (schema_version 1,
snake_case: execution_id, generation, owner{actor,host,kind}, task_sha,
target_ref, source_pushed, receipt_phase, worktree_removed,
local_branch_removed, remote_branch_removed, reclaim_*, exit_code, error).
resource_wait_duration_ms, validation_duration_ms, plan_duration_ms and
preparation_duration_ms stay in the document as explicit zeros: gz-git runs
no repository code, so nothing is admitted, validated or prepared.
Without an execution context, source_pushed and the three *_removed fields
report positive outcomes observed by this invocation; they do not create a
durable receipt or owner identity. With a receipt, its fields are authoritative.
False is not proof that an operation did not occur: positive evidence may be
unavailable. Verify actual Git/remote/filesystem state when reconciling a run.
Readiness refusal details are printed on stderr while JSON stdout remains
one protocol document.

When a complete execution context is refused before the target push because
target ownership was not acquired, pre_mutation_outcome
may carry a separately durable pre-mutation-outcome/v1 binding. Its absence
does not prove that no push occurred, and a receipt of any phase prevents a
negative outcome from being reused for that execution.

SIGINT or SIGTERM before the intent boundary (the receipt, or the push
without an execution context) stops the run, records no pre-mutation
outcome, and exits 2 with "interrupted before the target push". Past that
boundary a signal is ignored and the push, local fast-forward and reclaim
finish; only the first signal is handled, so a second one terminates gz-git
at once.

  2  usage or execution error
  3  integrated, but reclaim did not finish
  4  --expect-source/--expect-target: the approved commit pair changed; nothing was pushed

Usage:

Effect: mutating (worktree, refs, tracking-refs, remote, filesystem, config)

Flags:
      --controller-config string   explicit devbox/controller config; never searched automatically
      --direct-to-default          allow targeting the default branch when no integration branch exists
      --execution-id string        durable-evidence execution id; supply together with --generation, --owner-actor, --owner-host, --owner-kind and --expect-source, or not at all
      --expect-source string       fail with exit 4, before any push, unless the source is this full commit SHA
      --expect-target string       fail with exit 4, before any push, unless the target is this full commit SHA
      --generation string          exact runtime generation of this execution; opaque, compared exactly by receipt and cleanup
  -h, --help                       help for run
      --json                       print the machine JSON protocol document instead of the human report
      --no-fetch                   integrate from local tracking refs without fetching; remote delete failures fail closed
      --owner-actor string         logical actor executing the run (e.g. claude, celee)
      --owner-host string          logical device name (GIT_WORK_HOST / ce.workHost); never a hostname
      --owner-kind string          owner kind: agent or human
      --release                    promote the integration branch onto the default branch
      --target string              integration target (required when none can be resolved)

Global Flags:
      --profile string   override active profile (e.g., --profile work)
  -q, --quiet            quiet output (errors only)
  -v, --verbose          verbose output
